title: Neeraj Chandel v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
disposition: Recovery citation quashed; final assessment left open.
headnote: A recovery citation issued without a final assessment order and without a hearing under paragraph 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, was quashed. The petitioner may reply to the provisional assessment within seven days; respondent no. 2 may then pass a final assessment in accordance with law after considering those objections.
facts: Neeraj Chandel challenged, before the Lucknow Bench, a recovery citation dated 31 March 2023 issued by opposite party no. 4 for the electricity department. He said the citation had been issued without a final assessment order and without a hearing under paragraph 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Counsel for respondent nos. 2 and 3 accepted that no final assessment had been passed. A copy of the provisional assessment was given to his counsel in Court.

reusable_constructions.construction: A recovery citation issued before any final assessment order, and without the hearing under paragraph 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, is liable to be quashed.
After such a citation is quashed, the consumer must be allowed to object to the provisional assessment, and only then may the licensee pass a final assessment in accordance with law.

holding_units.holding: The recovery citation dated 31.03.2023, issued without a final assessment order and without an opportunity of hearing under paragraph 6.8 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, is quashed. The petitioner may submit a reply to the provisional assessment within seven days. Respondent no. 2 may thereafter pass a final assessment in accordance with law after considering those objections, and proceed further only if the occasion arises.

principle_tags.application: Counsel for the licensee accepted that the recovery citation had issued without a final assessment. The Court quashed that citation for want of the paragraph 6.8 hearing and a final assessment order.
The provisional assessment was supplied in Court, and the petitioner was allowed seven days to reply before any final assessment could be passed.

not_decided.point: Whether the provisional assessment is sustainable, and what final assessment if any should be made.
not_decided.note: Liberty was reserved to respondent no. 2 to pass a final assessment after considering the petitioner's objections.
